To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the tyrosine residue in the M2 protein cytoplasmic domain is critical for production of infectious virus particles and that the tyrosines at positions 71 and 76 are important for the formation of filamentus virus particles.
tyrosines at positions 76 and 71 in the M2 protein cytoplasmic domain are critical for infectious virus particle formation and that the Y76A mutant can be rescued by the S71Y mutation.

the Y76 residue in the M2 protein is critical for the production of filamentous infectious virus particles and that this residue is required for efficient nucleoprotein incorporation into virus particles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the influenza A M2 protein in the formation of virus particles and the assembly of the influenza virus genome into virus particles.
the molecular mechanisms of the assembly of infectious influenza A virus particles and how these mechanisms are affected by the antiviral drug, oseltamivir (Tamiflu).
the development of a new generation of vaccines and antivirals against influenza A virus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tyrosine residues at positions 71 and 76 of the M2 CT are essential for the formation of filament-like virus particles and the incorporation of NP into the virion.

tyrosines in the cytoplasmic domain of M2 play a critical role in virus assembly and that this role is mediated by the formation of disulphide bridges between the M2 cytosolic domains of two adjacent virions.
the tyrosines in the influenza A virus (IAV) M2 cytoplamic tail are critical for the production of IAV particles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tyrosine residues in the cytoplasmic domain of the influenza A M2 protein are critical for the production of infective virus particles.
the Y71 and Y76 residues in the influenza A virus (IAV) M2 protein cytoplasmic (C) tail are essential for the formation of virus particles.
the Y76A mutant virus has defects in M2 protein function that are not rescued by the S71Y mutant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tyrosine residues at positions 76 and 71 in the M2 protein cytoplasmic domain are critical for the production of virus particles that are infectious in vivo.
tyrosines in the cytoplasmic tails of the influenza A viruses M2 protein play a key role in the formation of infectious viral particles.
the tyrosines at positions 71 and 76 in the M2 protein cytoplasmic domain are important for the production of influenza A virus infectious virions and that the tyrosine at residue 76 is critical.
